title: Sweet Rhubarb Focaccia
changes_from_base: Sweet version: sugared rhubarb slices on top, brushed with their own reduced syrup and demerara instead of salt.
summary: A sweet focaccia topped with sugared rhubarb slices, glazed with their own pink syrup and crunchy demerara.
equipment: cling film or a clean tea towel

ingredients.item: rhubarb, thinly sliced on an angle

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, salt, warm water and 2 tbsp oil into a sticky dough, cover and rest 15 min.

steps.title: Folds
steps.text: Fold four times at 30 min intervals, until the dough is elastic and airy.

steps.title: Rhubarb
steps.text: During the last fold, toss the rhubarb with the caster sugar and leave 20-30 min, stirring now and then, until it has released a pink syrup. The sugar draws out the juice so the fruit stays in neat slices.

steps.title: Tin
steps.text: Pour 3 tbsp oil into the tin, add the dough and pat it out to about 1.5 cm thick, leaving a small gap at the edges. Cover and leave 45 min.

steps.title: Syrup
steps.text: Heat the oven to 230 °C (210 °C fan). Strain the rhubarb juices into a small pan and simmer 2-3 min, until thick. Dimple the dough, scatter the rhubarb over it, brush with the syrup and sprinkle with demerara.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 20-25 min, until golden brown and the rhubarb is tender; the centre reads about 96 °C. Cool 20 min, as the syrup is very hot, then cut into 12.

tips: Slice the rhubarb thinly on an angle so it softens in the bake.
Reduce the syrup only until it coats a spoon; it thickens more as it cools.
Use young, pink rhubarb for the best colour.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best on the day. Keep covered at room temperature for up to 1 day or in the fridge for up to 3 days; warm at 180 °C for 5 min.
